newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK ALPHA INVEST SAYS H1 NET UP 81.3 PCT.
newsitem.headline: GREEK ALPHA INVEST SAYS H1 NET UP 81.3 PCT.

text.p: Greek closed-end fund Alpha Invest said its half-year net profit rose 81.3 percent year-on-year to 5,785 million drachmas from 3,190 million.

The rise came on the back of a 185.1 percent improvement in gains from portfolio transactions to 4.71 billion drachmas from year-earlier 1.65 billion, despite a 19.1 percent setback in portfolio income to 1.44 billion drachmas, it said in a statement.
The fund's portfolio had unrealised gains of 8,155 million drachmas at end-June.
On June 30, 1997 the fund's common and preferred stock traded at a premium of 9.2 and 10.9 percent, respectively, to their net asset value (NAV) of 4,365 drachmas.
As of June 30, the fund was 70 percent invested in equities and 25 percent in fixed-income securities, the balance being cash and money market instruments, it said.
On the same date, Greek securities accounted for 83 percent of the fund's assets, with foreign securities making up 17 percent. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
